paragraphs: One-sentence judgment | this occupation is worth further verification only if you are willing to work in facilities and technical environments where radiation exposure is possible, can complete equipment operation, surveillance testing, measurement records, and tagging and isolation according to procedure, and accept the constraints of radiation safety training, dose monitoring, and position authorization; being drawn to the words nuclear or high-tech is not enough by itself.

Core output | linking equipment operation and test records, surveillance test results, radiation measurement and sample testing data, tagging and isolation records, and decontamination processes and waste handover into a traceable technical file: reviewable readings and records, not just a statement that the equipment is normal.

20—120 minute safe trial | use fictional equipment readings and radiation measurement records for one off-site exercise: judge 5 fictional reading sets as normal / needs re-check / should stop work and escalate, write out the procedure steps that must be checked and three anomaly conditions that must be reported immediately, and produce a record table containing measurement points, instrument numbers, background, readings, and the reviewer. The exercise uses only fictional data, and no real radiation measurement may be made, nor may any controlled area be entered or any equipment operated.

First threshold | confirm the authorization boundary first: who may operate and test nuclear equipment, who approves tagging and maintenance isolation, and who decides to stop work when a reading is abnormal. The United States has no single mandatory license covering all employers, but reactor operator licenses are managed separately by the NRC, and nuclear technician positions usually work under facility training and position authorization; radiation work units in China must obtain a radiation safety license, radiation workers must complete training assessment and personal dose monitoring, and those without an operator license may not operate nuclear facility control systems.

Nuclear Technicians (O*NET-SOC 19-4051.00, Nuclear Technicians) assist nuclear physicists, nuclear engineers, or other scientists in laboratory, power generation, and electricity production activities: operating and testing nuclear equipment according to nuclear equipment operating policies and procedures that ensure environmental safety, performing surveillance tests to judge equipment safety status, and monitoring reactor equipment performance to identify operating inefficiencies, hazards, or maintenance needs; tagging equipment awaiting repair and performing isolation, working according to radiation worker procedures to ensure personnel safety; using detectors or other instruments to measure the intensity and type of radiation in work areas, equipment, or materials, and calculating operating factors such as exposure time, dose, gamma intensity, or pressure using standard formulas and conversion tables; collecting and testing air, water, gas, or solid samples, determining and performing decontamination procedures, and installing and testing area radiation anomaly alarm devices.

entries: Equipment operation and testing | operate equipment according to nuclear equipment operating policies and procedures, test whether equipment operates normally, and modify, design, or maintain nuclear equipment used in operations as needed.

Surveillance testing | perform surveillance tests to judge the safety status of nuclear equipment, and monitor meters, gauges, or recording devices under the direction of nuclear laboratory personnel.
Performance monitoring and hazard identification | monitor reactor equipment performance and identify operating inefficiencies, hazards, or maintenance and repair needs.
Tagging and isolation | apply safety tags to equipment requiring maintenance, and coordinate isolation and restoration with maintenance personnel.

Radiation measurement and dose calculation | use detectors or other instruments to measure the intensity and type of radiation in work areas, equipment, or materials, calculate factors such as exposure time, dose, gamma intensity, or pressure using standard formulas and conversion tables, and warn maintenance personnel to evacuate when there is radiation danger.

Sample collection and decontamination | collect air, water, gas, or solid samples to determine radioactivity levels or confirm containment effectiveness, and determine and perform decontamination procedures according to the equipment and the nature of the contamination.

Accelerator and research support | perform testing, maintenance, repair, or upgrades on accelerator systems, and communicate with accelerator maintenance personnel about the readiness of support systems such as vacuum, water cooling, or radio frequency power.

paragraphs: The work is mainly facility site work and technical records: O*NET shows that 92% of this occupation is exposed to radiation, 95% wear common protective or safety equipment, and 64% wear specialized protective or safety equipment; 95% consider precision or accuracy extremely important, 80% report that the consequences of error are extremely serious, and 82% report being responsible for the health and safety of others, showing that the traceability of measurement and records is a basic requirement of the position.

The daily closed loop is confirming the work permit and equipment status, operating or performing surveillance tests according to procedure, re-checking readings and sample results, and recording and handing over; when a reading is abnormal, equipment fails, or isolation is incomplete, stop work first and then report and escalate according to procedure, rather than judging on behalf of maintenance or operations personnel that work can continue.

Insufficient evidence: O*NET has not yet published the new hire education composition distribution for 19-4051.00 (that page notes the occupation code profile is only partially available); this page cites only Job Zone 3 (SVP 6.0 to under 7.0), does not fill in education proportions, and the education composition may be referenced from the two sub-occupation pages 19-4051.01 and 19-4051.02.

Nuclear technicians should be distinguished from adjacent directions such as radiation monitoring technicians, reactor operators, instrumentation and control and electrical maintenance personnel, and nondestructive testing and industrial inspection positions by the main work object, control authority, and authorization boundary, rather than by similarity of job titles.

The comparison objects in this table come from the official tasks of O*NET 19-4051.00 and the official occupation descriptions and regulatory systems of adjacent occupations; O*NET 19-4051.01 Nuclear Equipment Operation Technicians and 19-4051.02 Nuclear Monitoring Technicians are two sub-directions under this occupation code, and the tasks of the nuclear monitoring direction have a more complete profile on the 19-4051.02 page.

The table below compares this occupation with adjacent directions on the same dimensions: main work object, core output, key differences, and selection signals; the comparison is for career exploration and does not represent mutual qualification recognition, automatic transfer, or a hiring promise.

The radiation monitoring technician direction takes the measurement, sampling, testing, and protection oversight of radiation and contamination as its main line, producing radiation protection files and radiation work permits; this occupation, while assisting engineering and research, also takes on equipment operation, testing, surveillance testing, and decontamination, and the two are different sub-codes under 19-4051 with different work emphasis and assessment paths.

If you would rather operate and test equipment, perform surveillance tests, and handle on-site technical problems, choose this occupation; if you would rather focus for the long term on radiation measurement, sampling, and dose records, you should choose the nuclear monitoring technician direction; if you want to operate nuclear facility control systems, you must separately obtain an operator license.
Beginners who want to start with tools first

First use public textbooks and simulated data to practise reading classification, unit conversion, and record table formats; treat tools as practice and review assistants, and do not use them to replace on-site judgment or safety conclusions.
Incumbent nuclear technician staff

Use tools for equipment ledger organization, test data checking, and procedure retrieval; keep the original readings, instrument numbers, and reviewer signatures, and anything entering the formal record must be traceable to the original data.
Facility radiation protection and operations managers

Clarify which tool outputs may enter test and monitoring records and which must be manually re-checked; keep version and audit information, and file according to the operating organization's training assessment and dose record system.
People transferring in from other industries

First make up the basics of radiation protection, measurement, and equipment safety, then check the applicable training assessment and position authorization against the target nuclear facility or nuclear technology use activity; the 2019 platform system cannot be extrapolated to all nuclear facility positions, and Class III sales and use has a 2021 self-examination arrangement.

O*NET19-4051.00 is a combined scope for nuclear technicians covering equipment support and monitoring; no one-to-one official mapping to the Chinese occupational classification has been obtained this round. Check against the real activity, the ecology and environment and health authorities, and the facility position requirements, and do not transplant the U.S. code as a Chinese statutory identity.

Scope comparison | the National Bureau of Statistics publishes the average wage of urban unit employed persons by industry category and does not list nuclear technicians separately; this page uses only the average values of the two categories Electricity, Heat, Gas, and Water Production and Supply and Scientific Research and Technical Services as reference, and marks them as category-level scope.

Verifiable reference | in 2025, the average annual wage of employed persons in urban non-private units in electricity, heat, gas, and water production and supply was 160,897 yuan, and in urban private units in the same category 66,451 yuan; in scientific research and technical services, non-private units 182,064 yuan and private units 83,560 yuan. The statistical scope covers legal entities with 5 or more employed persons in urban areas, and the survey excludes self-employed individuals and freelancers.

No Chinese wage distribution for this occupation has been obtained this round; the NBS industry average cannot replace an occupational median or percentile. Units producing, selling, and using isotopes and ray devices are checked for radiation safety permits under the applicable activity; nuclear facilities are managed under nuclear safety permits, and not all nuclear technology units can be uniformly called radiation license holders. Operating control systems requires the corresponding license and authorization; the regulations allow training under temporary authorization supervised by a licensed person for those not yet licensed, and this cannot be extrapolated to independent operation. Health training before taking up a post is not less than 4 days, with two sessions no more than 2 years apart and each not less than 2 days; the ecology and environment assessment for nuclear technology use applies the 2019 reform and 2021 classification separately, and only Class III ray device sales and use personnel are assessed by the unit itself (result valid 5 years), not uniformly on the platform. Personal external exposure monitoring is generally 30 days and at most 90 days, and lifelong retention of dose records follows the health authority measures.

paragraphs: The key signals of fit for this occupation are: being able to maintain protection and recording habits over the long term, being willing to repeat measurements and tests according to procedure, being able to stop work and escalate when a reading is abnormal, and being able to hand over clearly with maintenance and operations personnel; interest codes and work style labels cannot determine fit, and you must return to real tasks and mentoring evaluation.

Interest codes and work styles come from the O*NET 19-4051.00 summary (the page notes that the occupation code profile is only partially available) and are exploratory evidence; the fit signals and trial design on this page are editorial synthesis and do not constitute selection standards, ability assessment, or a hiring promise.

Boundary statement | this list cannot replace the facility's radiation protection system, radiation safety license conditions, equipment operation and tagging procedures, overhaul isolation plans, or emergency plans. The main risks center on: wrong reading or contamination judgments, dose calculation and record deviations, equipment operation and testing departing from procedure, incomplete tagging and isolation, incomplete decontamination and improper radioactive waste disposal, and operating equipment beyond training and position authorization; control requirements should be tailored to the facility license conditions and position authorization.

The main risks are distorted equipment or radiation readings, test deviations, incomplete isolation, decontamination and waste disposal, and dose overexposure; control them through applicable calibration and verification, re-testing, institutional re-check, dose monitoring, health examinations, and traceable records. Two-person verification is an institution-applicable measure and is not a uniform headcount requirement of the cited health law.

The O*NET work context table is a 0—100 standardized score: radiation 92, common protection 95, specialized protection 64, accuracy 95, consequences of error 80, responsibility for others' safety 82; these are not a 92% of staff exposed or an incident probability, and the scores cannot be read as the proportion of a response option. Legal bases apply separately by nuclear facility and nuclear technology use activity, health training, and monitoring systems.

Equipment testers, monitoring and sampling personnel, decontamination personnel, and maintenance personnel who rely on isolation / measurement results are affected; no seniority or temporary support comparison data has been obtained this round, and it is not asserted that newcomers are most likely to skip steps.

Possible consequences | a wrong reading or contamination judgment puts personnel at unnecessary radiation risk, and incomplete decontamination or improper waste disposal causes residual contamination and illegal transfer; incomplete isolation may cause injury to maintenance personnel or accidental equipment movement; missing records and dose files affect occupational health traceability and regulatory compliance.

Recruitment sample (editorial compilation) | this page does not copy any single employer's recruitment announcement; the following are position sample points compiled from O*NET tasks, industry requirements, and the Chinese radiation safety management system, used to understand the actual position requirements and not representing an open vacancy. Typical requirements include: mastery of nuclear equipment operation and testing, surveillance test execution and records, radiation measurement and dose calculation, sample collection and decontamination, and tagging and isolation coordination; ability to use protective equipment according to procedure and to accept training assessment and personal dose monitoring.

Entry signal | the most common entry combination for this occupation is related professional education or facility training plus position authorization; O*NET notes that the occupation code profile is only partially available and does not publish the new hire education composition distribution, so no education proportions are provided, and the actual requirements follow the target facility and employer announcements.

Entry exercise data (editorial design) | a fictional training data package: a record table with 6 measurement point readings and instrument background, an equipment surveillance test record template, and a tagging and isolation list for equipment awaiting repair. The exercise requires completing reading classification, test record filling, and isolation condition checking according to procedure; the data and templates are all fictional, correspond to no real facility, and do not constitute onboarding or operating authorization.

paragraphs: Units producing, selling, and using isotopes and ray devices are checked for radiation safety permits under the applicable activity; nuclear facilities are managed under nuclear safety permits, and not all nuclear technology units can be uniformly called radiation license holders. Operating control systems requires the corresponding license and authorization; the regulations allow training under temporary authorization supervised by a licensed person for those not yet licensed, and this cannot be extrapolated to independent operation.

Boundary statement two | radiation protection is a continuing obligation: pre-post training is not less than 4 days, two training sessions are no more than 2 years apart, the external exposure personal dose monitoring period is generally 30 days and at most 90 days, and personal dose records are kept for life.

Boundary statement three | equipment operation and testing must be carried out according to procedure and authorization: equipment that fails testing or whose isolation is incomplete should stop being used and be reported, and acceptance criteria must not be relaxed because of schedule pressure.

Boundary statement four | nuclear technicians do not replace the decisions of the shift operations supervisor and the radiation protection officer: when a reading is abnormal, a contamination judgment is uncertain, or the situation exceeds the authorization scope, stop work and submit the matter to the corresponding responsible person according to procedure.

Capability progression should start with supervised learning of radiation protection, instrument use, and record norms, then after obtaining training assessment and position authorization independently take on equipment testing, surveillance testing, and radiation measurement, then participate in anomaly handling, decontamination, and overhaul support, and finally enter technical guidance and procedure improvement; each step is premised on training assessment records, dose monitoring records, and facility position authorization.

details: Article Five: the nuclear facility operating organization bears overall responsibility for nuclear safety. details: Article Three: only those holding an Operator License may work on operating nuclear facility control systems, and only those holding a Senior Operator License may work on operating or directing others to operate; personnel without a license being trained on the control system must obtain temporary authorization and be supervised by an operator.

risks.consequence: Dose limit judgments are distorted, and occupational health traceability and compliance checks cannot be supported
risks.mitigation: Calculate using a substantiated formula, calibration, and measurement conditions, re-check according to institutional procedure, and keep dose files in accordance with law

risks.title: Dose calculation and record deviations

risks.affected_roles: Positions responsible for equipment testing and surveillance testing
risks.consequence: Equipment runs while faulty or is released in error, threatening facility and personnel safety
risks.mitigation: Test according to procedure, check acceptance criteria, and stop use and report when they fail
risks.scenario: Failing to execute testing and surveillance testing according to the specified procedure, or continuing to use equipment after a failed test
risks.title: Equipment testing or surveillance testing failure

risks.affected_roles: Positions performing tagging and isolation and maintenance coordination
risks.consequence: Maintenance personnel are injured or equipment moves accidentally
risks.mitigation: Tag and isolate according to procedure, with the permit issuer and the maintenance officer jointly confirming restoration conditions
risks.scenario: Lockout, tagging, and isolation measures are incomplete, or isolation is removed before restoration conditions are confirmed
risks.title: Incomplete tagging and isolation

risks.affected_roles: Positions exposed to decontamination work and radioactive waste
risks.consequence: Residual contamination and illegal transfer affecting personnel and environmental safety
risks.mitigation: Decontaminate and re-test according to procedure, and mark, register, and hand over radioactive waste properly
risks.scenario: Applying for release without re-testing after decontamination, or failing to classify, mark, and properly hand over radioactive waste
risks.title: Incomplete decontamination or improper radioactive waste disposal

risks.affected_roles: All technical positions and temporary support personnel
risks.consequence: Acting beyond authority brings personnel safety and compliance risk and is punishable by law
risks.mitigation: Work within the scope of training assessment and position authorization, and refer matters beyond scope to the corresponding responsible person or competent department

components.definition_block: Nuclear Technicians (O*NET-SOC 19-4051.00, Nuclear Technicians) assist nuclear physicists, nuclear engineers, or other scientists in laboratory, power generation, and electricity production activities: operating and testing nuclear equipment according to operating policies and procedures that ensure environmental safety, performing surveillance tests to judge equipment safety status, monitoring reactor equipment performance to identify inefficiencies, hazards, or maintenance needs; applying safety tags to equipment awaiting repair and supporting isolation; working according to radiation worker procedures to protect personnel safety; using detectors or other instruments to measure the intensity and type of radiation in work areas, equipment, or materials and calculating operating factors such as exposure time, dose, gamma intensity, or pressure using standard formulas and conversion tables; collecting and testing air, water, gas, or solid samples, determining and performing decontamination procedures, and installing and testing area radiation anomaly alarm devices; the actually executable scope is determined by training assessment, the radiation safety license, and facility position authorization.

description.text: Nuclear Technicians (O*NET 19-4051.00) assist nuclear engineers and researchers in operating, testing, and maintaining nuclear equipment, performing surveillance tests, measuring radiation, collecting samples, and performing decontamination; this page explains their tasks, preparation requirements, Chinese and U.S. qualification and authorization boundaries, and the wage and employment statistical scope.

subject.name: Nuclear Technicians
subject.summary: Nuclear Technicians (O*NET-SOC 19-4051.00, Nuclear Technicians) assist nuclear physicists, nuclear engineers, or other scientists in laboratory, power generation, and electricity production activities: operating, testing, and maintaining nuclear equipment according to nuclear equipment operating policies and radiation worker procedures, performing surveillance tests to judge equipment safety status, monitoring reactor equipment performance and identifying inefficiencies, hazards, or maintenance needs, tagging equipment awaiting repair and implementing isolation, using detectors or other instruments to measure the intensity and type of radiation in work areas, equipment, or materials, calculating operating factors such as exposure time, dose, and gamma intensity using standard formulas, collecting and testing air, water, gas, or solid samples, performing decontamination, and setting up area radiation anomaly alarm devices. This page uses only official sources to explain the occupational scope, tasks, Chinese and U.S. statistical scope, and authorization boundaries.
